Remove `async-trait` and use AFIT(Async Fn In Trait) and RPITIT(Return Position Impl Trait In Traits).

comments.body: Could you change these impls that were previously non-`async` fns returning `BoxFuture` to still be non-`async` but return `-> impl Future`? The extra `.await` actually means an extra level of laziness for all function parameters, which I'm pretty sure increases the future stack size.
The previous comment does not apply here where we returned a boxed async block before.
Is the `+ '_` needed? I think the impl trait return type should capture the `&mut self` lifetime implicitly.
Same thing here about `async fn` vs. `fn -> impl Future`.
Why did you change this? It means that an inherent `from_request_parts` would be called here if it exists in addition to the one from a `FromRequestParts` impl, which I don't think is right.

Because an error occurs if I don't change this.
```bash
error[E0282]: type annotations needed
   --> axum-extra/src/either.rs:250:17
    |
250 |                 FromRequestParts::from_request_parts(parts, state).await.map(Self::$last)
    |                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ cannot infer type
...
275 | impl_traits_for_either!(Either8 => [E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7], E8);
    | -------------------------------------------------------------------- in this macro invocation
    |
    = note: this error originates in the macro `impl_traits_for_either` (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0282`.
error: could not compile `axum-extra` (lib) due to 7 previous errors
```
This new paramter doesn't seem to be used.
Related to the first review comment, these changes don't seem to be necessary.

This should fix the problem you were talking about:

```suggestion
                    <#field_ty as ::axum::extract::FromRequest<#trait_generics, _>>::from_request(req, state)
```
Oh, I guess I was wrong (seeing the revert diff), I probably mistook a `}` to be a level higher. Anyways, if the simpler version works, let's go with that.
